newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom charge helps hoist NZ bluechips by close.
newsitem.headline: Telecom charge helps hoist NZ bluechips by close.

text.p: LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +31.15 at 2,484.97

Action in a handful of top line stocks dominated business on the New Zealand stock exchange on Wednesday, with the wider market still overshadowed by some nervousness on the volatile currency and domestic debt market. Brokers said a bounding recovery by Telecom, which added a thumping 25 cents to close at NZ$7.53, did most of the work in lifting the bluechip indices well over one percent. Telecom is the most heavily-weighted share in the top-40 index.
The NZSE-40 closed up 31.15 points, or 1.27 percent, at 2,484.97. The smallcap index, by contrast, closed flat while the mid-cap index ended slightly weaker.
Volume worth a total of $75 million was dominated by Telecom, which accounted for nearly a quarter of the total.
Brokers said that after Telecom's equally rapid decline in the last two weeks, from all-time highs around $7.90 to Monday's $7.20, there had been a spell of buying that corrected the price.
"They had a pretty big fall, but it's probably gone a bit too far on the upside now," one senior broker said.
He said Telecom's sensitivity to the bond market had been clearly shown during the recent fall and noted the buying phase had begun when strength returned to that market on Tuesday.
A global bond rally, fuelled in part by the comments of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan during his Humphrey Hawkins testimony, supported NZ bond gains again today.
Nevertheless, the big gains posted by the Dow overnight failed to ignite this market across the board, dealers said.

Big volumes in bluechip brewer Lion Nathan, up five cents at $3.85, and forest products group Fletcher Paper, up two at $3.39, took up another chunk of the overall trading total and a large number of the top 40 ended unchanged or a cent higher or lower.
